# Maya's Storybooks

> Free bilingual (English + Nepali) picture-book stories from Nepal for children ages 3–7. All stories are free to read on this website. No ads. No accounts. The Maya's Storybook app is coming soon for iPhone and Android.

## What this site is

- A free read-aloud storybook website for children ages 3–7, rooted in real festivals and places in Nepal.
- Every book is available in English and in Nepali, with read-aloud narration in the web player.
- Free forever: the stories, the read-aloud, and the games. No ads. No accounts. No subscriptions.
- The app is coming soon. Visitors can leave a parent's email address to be notified once, at launch.

## Books (all 20, all free)

- Book 1: The Dog Who Wore Marigolds — A scruffy stray crashes Kukur Tihar — and one little girl's marigold garland changes everything. The story that started it all. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book1
- Book 2: Maya and the Temple Monkey — A cheeky monkey snatches Maya's marigold offering at Swayambhunath — the chase up the 365 steps ends in a gentle surprise about kindness and sharing. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book2
- Book 3: Maya and the Rhino of Chitwan — A jungle safari turns into a rescue mission when Maya meets a baby rhino in trouble. Brave hearts come in small sizes. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book3
- Book 4: Maya and the Clay Diyo — Grandmother's clay oil lamp won't light — until Maya discovers what makes a tiny flame brave enough to glow. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book4
- Book 5: Maya and the Garden of Peace — In the quiet gardens of Lumbini, Maya plants a tiny bodhi sapling — and makes a wish too soft for words. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book5
- Book 6: Maya and the Baby Yak — High in the mountains, Maya and Moti follow tiny hoofprints to find a lost baby yak — and Moti earns a brass bell for his tracking. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book6
- Book 7: Maya and Indra Jatra — Drums, masked dancers, and the living goddess roll through Basantapur — and Maya lights a lamp for someone she loves and misses. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book7
- Book 8: Maya and the Honey Hunters — On a cliff tall as a hundred houses, Bir Dai the honey hunter climbs a bamboo ladder — and Maya tastes honey like sunshine and flowers. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book8
- Book 9: Maya and the Yeti's Sneeze — A giant sneeze shakes the snowy mountain — and Maya, Grandmother, and Moti nurse a shy, shaggy yeti back to health with tea and the biggest red scarf. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book9
- Book 10: Maya and the Kite Thief of Dashain — Someone keeps stealing kites from the Dashain sky. Maya follows the string to a thief with a surprising secret. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book10
- Book 11: Maya and the Bhai Tika Brother — Maya has no brother for Bhai Tika — so she chooses one with her heart, and paints seven colors of wishes on his forehead. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book11
- Book 12: Maya and the Monk of Boudhanath — Cross about a chewed drawing, Maya sweeps the stupa courtyard with an old monk — and writes her anger on a paper prayer flag for the wind to carry away. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book12
- Book 13: Maya and the Lake of Pokhara — On Phewa Lake the mountains are painted twice — once in the sky, once in the water — and Moti barks at the little white dog in the lake. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book13
- Book 14: Maya and the Road to Everest — One brave step at a time, Maya walks the mountain trail all the way to Everest Base Camp — and ties a blessed kata scarf to the prayer flags. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book14
- Book 15: Maya's Big Festival — Maya invites every friend she ever made — the yeti, the kite boy, the monk, and Bir Dai — to one big festival in her lane. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book15
- Book 16: Maya and the Goddess's Courage — When the big boys won't share the great Dashain swing, Grandmother's tale of goddess Durga gives Maya her bravest word: “Stop.” Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book16
- Book 17: Maya and the Monkey King — Grandmother tells of a monkey king who became a bridge so his whole troop could escape — and Maya shares her biggest mango, just like him. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book17
- Book 18: Maya and the Two Arrows — A scraped knee is one arrow — but a whole grumpy afternoon is a second arrow Maya shoots herself, until Grandmother's old story helps her put it down. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book18
- Book 19: Maya and the Wind of Mustang — The Mustang wind steals Maya's red scarf — and teaches her that some things you catch by letting go. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book19
- Book 24: Maya and the Roof of the World — A faded photograph sends Maya and Grandmother over the roof of the world to Lhasa — to find Dolma, Grandmother's best friend of sixty years ago. Read: https://mayastorybooks.com/books/book24

## Characters

- Maya: a six-year-old girl who lives with her Grandmother in a hill village. Kind, generous, brave, and curious.
- Moti: a puppy whose name means "Pearl" in Nepali. A scruffy stray Maya rescued on Kukur Tihar.
- Grandmother: the warm heart of Maya's world; her bedtime tales become real adventures. She never rushes and never scolds.
- Characters: https://mayastorybooks.com/wiki

## Paperbacks

Six stories are also available as paperbacks on Amazon: Books 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, and 16. The other books have no paperback edition.

## Privacy

- The website counts anonymous story plays (which book was opened, and in which language). No personal data is collected, and nothing is shared with third parties.
- The app's privacy policy is at https://mayastorybooks.com/privacy/mayas-storybook
